# VBA grammar provenance and local changes

The grammar implementation is derived from
[`harumiWeb/tree-sitter-vba`](https://github.com/harumiWeb/tree-sitter-vba/tree/a67fd2ddeb577730c363cbbdb1405274594d8a3f),
revision `a67fd2ddeb577730c363cbbdb1405274594d8a3f`, metadata version `0.14.1`.
`LICENSE` is the upstream MIT license. `THIRD_PARTY_LICENSE.md` describes separately
licensed upstream examples; none of those fixture collections are included here.
The Cargo manifest and Rust binding are local additions, not a published crate.
The local `tree-sitter.json` describes only the included VBA grammar and Rust
binding; absent VB6, highlighting queries, and other bindings are not advertised.

The upstream shared grammar factory and VBA entry point are preserved in their
original directory structure. Native tables and headers are generated with
Tree-sitter CLI `0.26.8`, ABI `15`, from the `vba` directory:

```text
tree-sitter generate --abi 15 --js-runtime native
```

The original shared grammar SHA-256 is
`568789348922d4e387c10ff580290c09eb434d0ce3f2389b29aca7a7af18a660`.
The unmodified VBA parser generated by that command has SHA-256
`1ec8fc0c44c49fd15da2174a4db92824c4be048c074689e8e0b8962a2ab81e0a`.

## Statement identity correction

VBA accepts explicit assignments and procedure-local subroutine control flow.
The upstream grammar restricted `Let`, `LSet`, `RSet`, `GoSub`, and `Return` to
its VB6 variant. VBA input could therefore parse without errors while incorrectly
classifying those keywords as called procedure names. These productions are now
available in block, inline, and numbered VBA statement contexts. `ReDim`
declarators also retain their optional per-array `As` clause.

Language references: Microsoft VBA
[Let](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/let-statement),
[LSet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/lset-statement),
[RSet](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/rset-statement),
[GoSub/Return](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/gosubreturn-statement),
and [ReDim](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/vba/language/reference/user-interface-help/redim-statement).
The grammar recognizes syntax; it does not establish runtime type compatibility
or simulate assignments, allocation, or the subroutine stack.

`tests/native-grammars/tests/vba.rs` checks exact statement kinds and source spans,
exported class and procedure identities, malformed syntax, byte-edit/recovery
equivalence, and native cancellation/reset. No global runtime limits change.
The other upstream dialect gates remain unchanged; native parse success is not
proof of full VBA/VB6 coverage or installed Rootlight semantic support.

## Numeric tokens and comparison associativity

The numeric token rule includes `D`/`d` exponents and octal prefixes with an
optional `O`/`o`, including bare `&77`. These are literal spellings in Microsoft
[MS-VBAL section 3.3.2 Number Tokens](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/microsoft_general_purpose_programming_languages/ms-vbal/685ad840-accb-4bdb-8bfd-f3d88498547a),
not extensions inferred from string-to-number coercion.

VBA comparisons may be left operands of subsequent comparisons, matching
[MS-VBAL section 5.6.9.1 Operator Precedence and Associativity](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/microsoft_general_purpose_programming_languages/ms-vbal/24cb214a-ef26-4e36-973d-43f715c8b127).
The existing VB6 call-target assignment precedence also applies to VBA so
`items(index) = value > 0` remains an assignment rather than an implicit call
with `(index) = value > 0` as its argument. The precedence is limited to
call-shaped targets; plain-name assignment recovery is unchanged.

The authored native contracts check exact numeric spans in initializers,
defaults, assignments and arguments, left-nested comparison nodes, and
assignment versus implicit-call identity. These corrections do not evaluate
numeric values, perform coercion, or prove runtime array or call targets.
